reports.title: Microsoft 365 Security Controls – State Entities
reports.finding: The audit identified gaps in tenant baselines, identity protection, data loss prevention, logging and email protection. It assessed cloud services, not desktop Office applications.
reports.assessment: Test effective policies across users, guests, privileged identities and unmanaged devices. Inspect exclusions and shared-tenant dependencies; retrieve actual audit events and demonstrate restoration of security configuration.

reports.title: Implementation of the Essential Eight Cyber Security Controls
reports.finding: The audit found that self-assessments often overstated implementation. Unapproved code, incomplete authentication coverage and ineffective recovery testing were recurring issues.
reports.assessment: Demonstrate enforcement on representative devices and exception groups before claiming maturity. Use the applicable ACSC edition for thresholds; this audit assessed December 2022 self-reports.

reports.title: Universities and TAFEs 2025 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.finding: Unscanned internet-facing systems, incomplete endpoint enrolment, retained contractor access and ineffective network isolation illustrated weaknesses in operational coverage.
reports.assessment: Reconcile asset, agent and identity inventories using independent populations. Include servers, contractors, unknown devices and provider assurance in samples; retest previously unresolved findings.

reports.title: Local Government 2025 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.finding: Examples included unmonitored database changes, remote administration without MFA and permanent vendor privileges. Good practice included patch-compliance review and restrictions on unmanaged cloud access.
reports.assessment: Inspect direct database access as well as application roles. Verify vendor expiry, remote sign-in enforcement and investigation of data-change events; test device restrictions using an unmanaged test device.

reports.title: State Government 2025 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.sector: WA State government; excludes tertiary audits still in progress
reports.finding: Access weaknesses included former staff retaining active accounts, financial approval limits not enforced in applications and administrative accounts with conflicting transaction authority.
reports.assessment: Compare configured permissions with approved delegations. Use synthetic transactions to test approval boundaries and segregation of duties; reconcile departure dates with actual disablement and subsequent sign-ins.

reports.title: PathWest’s Laboratory Information System
reports.finding: The report identified encryption, access review, logging, vulnerability oversight and recovery weaknesses affecting a clinical system and its dependencies. It also records remediation undertaken after the audit.
reports.assessment: Trace protection across application, database, server and interfaces. Include supplier access, legacy components and a dependency-aware recovery test; do not infer present performance from historical findings.

reports.title: State Government 2023-24 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.finding: Recurring weaknesses included inadequate provider assurance, network segregation and continuity plans that were outdated or untested.
reports.assessment: Verify customer responsibilities from provider assurance reports. Demonstrate separation between network zones and restore the complete business service against agreed recovery objectives, including third-party dependencies.

reports.title: Local Government 2023-24 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.finding: Examples included unrecorded laptops, unmanaged contractor onboarding and exit, stale continuity plans and gaps in server-room access monitoring.
reports.assessment: Reconcile physical stocktakes with management inventories. Sample contractors separately from employees, check refresher training and access cancellation, and trace physical-access exceptions to follow-up.

reports.title: Child Protection Case Management System – Assist
reports.sector: WA Department of Communities; application audit
reports.finding: The audit identified excessive record access, sensitive copies outside approved systems, unmasked production data in test environments, limited database monitoring and untested recovery dependencies.
reports.assessment: Test record-level authorisation with synthetic cases. Inspect test-data masking, approved collaboration locations and both application and database audit trails. Validate out-of-hours supplier recovery commitments.

reports.title: Local Government 2022-23 – Information Systems Audit Results
reports.finding: An application-control example allowed users to write into trusted execution locations. Other findings concerned excessive privileges, incomplete MFA and insufficient cloud-provider assurance.
reports.assessment: Check write permissions on allowlisted paths and attempt benign unapproved code from a standard-user profile. Test complete recovery to a consistent point, rather than relying only on successful file restores.

reports.title: Local Government IT Disaster Recovery Planning
reports.sector: WA local government; six audited entities
reports.finding: Recovery plans and supplier agreements did not consistently establish how services would be restored within business needs. Testing was insufficient to demonstrate that plans would work.
reports.assessment: Time an agreed recovery exercise including replacement infrastructure, identity, applications and data. Reconcile supplier delivery times and after-hours responsibilities with the plan and business recovery targets.

reports.title: Information Systems Audit – Local Government 2021-22
reports.finding: Many findings remained unresolved from earlier years. The report introduced ten capability categories, separating information security into five areas to expose operational weaknesses more clearly.
reports.assessment: Trace repeat findings to accountable owners, implemented changes and independent retests. Evaluate interacting access, endpoint and network weaknesses together; do not substitute a policy document for operating evidence.

reports.title: Information Systems Audit – State Government 2021-22
reports.finding: Findings included misconfigured email authentication, untrusted code execution, retained access, unmanaged mobile-device risks and inadequate separation of production and test environments.
reports.assessment: Verify mail authentication through received-message headers, not DNS records alone. Test device posture and environment separation, and confirm that access removal reaches connected applications.
